## Exercise 10.1

I made this sbatch file, chansing N and ntasks (1,16), (4,4), (16,1).
Probably, when the ntasks is lower, the parallel processing is more inefficient because of increased communication cost over different nodes.

```bash
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH -J homework10

#SBATCH -N 1
#SBATCH --ntasks-per-node=16


#SBATCH -N 4
#SBATCH --ntasks-per-node=4

#SBATCH -N 16
#SBATCH --ntasks-per-node=1

#SBATCH --mem=2048
#SBATCH -t 00:10:00

module load py-mpi4py/3.1.3
module load py-numpy/1.22.4

hostname #prints the node's name 
echo '# nodes: ----------------'
printenv SLURM_NNODES
echo '# tasks per node: -------------'
printenv SLURM_NTASKS_PER_NODE

cd "$SLURM_SUBMIT_DIR"

python3 a10_collect.py
```

I just re-used homework07 data collection code, and made a10_collect.py.
This saves `a10_strong.csv` and `a10_weak.csv`.
So in the HPC, just running this python file and saving these csv files. 
After the job finishes, run `quarto render homework10.qmd` to make this pdf and visualizations in the local environment.

N=2304 is divisible by 1, 4, 9, and 16.
We use one warm-up and five runs, reporting the median maximum-rank time.

```{python}
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from IPython.display import Markdown, display

layouts = [(1, 16), (4, 4), (16, 1)]
summaries = []
plt.rcParams.update({"font.size": 8})
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(7, 2.7))
for ax, (nodes, tasks) in zip(axes, layouts):
    label = f"{nodes} nodes × {tasks} tasks/node"
    raw = pd.read_csv(f"a10_{nodes}_{tasks}_strong.csv")
    process_counts = sorted(raw.P.unique())
    N = int(raw.N.iloc[0])
    display(Markdown(f"### {label}"))
    display(Markdown(raw.to_markdown(index=False)))
    summary = raw.groupby("P").total.agg(
        median="median", minimum="min", maximum="max"
    ).reset_index()
    T1 = summary.loc[summary.P == 1, "median"].iloc[0]
    summary["speedup"] = T1 / summary["median"]
    summary["efficiency"] = summary.speedup / summary.P
    summaries.append(summary)
    display(Markdown(summary.to_markdown(index=False)))
    ax.plot(summary.P, summary.speedup, "o-", label="Measured")
    ax.plot(process_counts, process_counts, "k:", label="Ideal S(P)=P")
    ax.set_title(f"{label}")
    ax.set_xlabel("MPI processes (P)")
    ax.set_ylabel("Relative speedup")
    ax.set_xticks(process_counts)
    ax.grid()
    ax.legend(fontsize=7)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

As we expected, 1 nodes x 16 tasks pair shows the similar speedup that I got in the homework07.  
However, 4 nodes x 4 tasks pair shows the similar speedup until P=4, then after because of the communication between nodes, the efficiency significantly drops.  
The 16 nodes x 1 tasks pair shows the drop from P=4.

## Exercise 10.2

```{python}
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(7, 2.7), sharey=True)
for ax, (nodes, tasks), summary in zip(axes, layouts, summaries):
    ax.plot(summary.P, summary.efficiency, "o-")
    ax.axhline(1, color="black", linestyle=":", label="Ideal E(P)=1")
    ax.set_title(f"{nodes} nodes × {tasks} tasks/node")
    ax.set_xlabel("MPI processes (P)")
    ax.set_ylabel("Efficiency")
    ax.set_xticks(summary.P)
    ax.set_yscale("log")
    ax.grid()
    ax.legend(fontsize=7)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

These plots are essentially the same as the previous plot. The y-axis scale is the same across 3 plots for easy comparison.  
The efficiency drops significantly when it starts communicating with different nodes.

## Exercise 10.3

We follow the assignment's N=n*P rule with n=144 and the same timing protocol.
For dense matrix multiplication, this rule does not keep computation per process constant.

```{python}
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(7, 2.7), sharey=True)
for ax, (nodes, tasks) in zip(axes, layouts):
    label = f"{nodes} nodes × {tasks} tasks/node"
    raw = pd.read_csv(f"a10_{nodes}_{tasks}_weak.csv")
    n = int(raw.N.iloc[0] // raw.P.iloc[0])
    display(Markdown(f"### {label}"))
    display(Markdown(raw.to_markdown(index=False)))
    weak = raw.groupby(["P", "N"]).total.agg(
        median="median", minimum="min", maximum="max"
    ).reset_index()
    T1 = weak.loc[weak.P == 1, "median"].iloc[0]
    weak["scaled_efficiency"] = T1 / weak["median"]
    display(Markdown(weak.to_markdown(index=False)))
    ax.plot(weak.P, weak.scaled_efficiency, "o-")
    ax.set_title(f"{label}")
    ax.set_xlabel("MPI processes (P)")
    ax.set_ylabel("Scaled efficiency")
    ax.set_yscale("log")
    ax.set_xticks(weak.P)
    ax.grid()
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

This is an interesting result. The y-axis scale is the same across 3 plots for easy comparison.  
At P=4, all 3 settings show the similar efficiency.  
This suggests that communication between nodes introduces substantial overhead when N is large. However, when N is sufficiently small, the inter-node communication overhead is comparable to that of intra-node communication.
